analysis.title: Global Macro Chart of the Day (#194): Tech accounts for 55% of global export growth
key_insights: Tech accounts for 55% of the annual growth in global exports while making up roughly 27% of global exports by value, up from 22% in 2022.

UBS's 'Tech' export aggregate came to nearly $6 trillion over the last 12 months. It includes telecommunications equipment, TVs, computers, optical and medical instruments, photographic equipment and other electronics.
A large part of the growth in the Tech aggregate comes from AI-related trade, including automatic data processing machines and semiconductors.
The AI supply chain is concentrated in trade terms: two buyers and five suppliers account for 80% of all AI trade, per an earlier UBS note.
UBS estimates hyperscaler capex at close to $1 trillion in 2026 (3% of US GDP), rising to $1.75 trillion in 2027 (a bit over 5% of GDP). Much of AI trade is the counterpart of this capex.
For scale, 172 of the 193 UN member countries have a GDP smaller than $1 trillion.

risk_factors: Global export growth is concentrated in tech and AI-related goods, so a pullback in hyperscaler capex would hit trade growth.
The AI trade is concentrated in two buyers and five suppliers, which concentrates the exposure.
